LESSON: READING 8.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: POETRY

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 8
Topic 8.4: Reading 8.4.1 Intensive Reading: Poetry
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 8.4.1 Intensive Reading: Poetry, part of Strand 8 in Grade 7 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why are human characters important in poetry?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. read a given poem and identify the human characters,

2. search online and offline for adjectives that can be used to describe characters,

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. read a given poem and identify the human characters,
2. search online and offline for adjectives that can be used to describe characters,

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 8.4.1 Intensive Reading: Poetry together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: It is enhanced the learner contributes to group decision-making by participating actively

in the discussion on what each character does or says in each poem.

• Learning to learn : It is developed as the learner builds on their own learning experiences while associating the human

characters in the poem with real life situations.

Values:
• Peace is enhanced as the learner works in groups to execute different tasks in the poem.

• Love is nurtured as the learner shows a caring attitude when working with peers to relate human characters to real life.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Social cohesion is enhanced as the learner role plays a given poem to bring out the characters’ actions.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner relate the concepts learnt in poetry to the study of poems in Kiswahili.
